pointers.sentence: A **project state**, a `ProjectState`, is a project's models held as data: a dictionary of **model states**, each a `ModelState` with one model's fields, options, bases and managers and no class (`django/db/migrations/state.py:ProjectState`, `django/db/migrations/state.py:ModelState`).

A **project state**, a `ProjectState`, is a project's models held as data: a dictionary of **model states**, each a `ModelState` with one model's fields, options, bases and managers and no class (`django/db/migrations/state.py:ProjectState`, `django/db/migrations/state.py:ModelState`).

Or it can be read off the model classes: `ProjectState.from_apps` asks a registry for its models, those swapped out included and those a many-to-many field made for itself left out, and files what `ModelState.from_model` makes of each (`django/db/migrations/state.py:ProjectState.from_apps`). makemigrations makes its to-state so, from the main registry ([The makemigrations command](makemigrations.md)).
`ModelState.from_model` makes a model state from a model class (`django/db/migrations/state.py:ModelState.from_model`).

`from_model` takes the model's own fields, `Options.local_fields` and then `Options.local_many_to_many`, and files `Field.clone` of each under its name (`django/db/models/options.py:Options.add_field`, `django/db/models/fields/__init__.py:Field.clone`).

`from_model` takes the model's own fields, `Options.local_fields` and then `Options.local_many_to_many`, and files `Field.clone` of each under its name (`django/db/models/options.py:Options.add_field`, `django/db/models/fields/__init__.py:Field.clone`).

The clone has no `Field.model`, and a relation in it names its target by a string, which is how a relation deconstructs (`django/db/models/fields/related.py:ForeignObject.deconstruct`, `django/db/models/fields/related.py:ManyToManyField.deconstruct`; [A field: the base class](../models/fields.md)).

The clone has no `Field.model`, and a relation in it names its target by a string, which is how a relation deconstructs (`django/db/models/fields/related.py:ForeignObject.deconstruct`, `django/db/models/fields/related.py:ManyToManyField.deconstruct`; [A field: the base class](../models/fields.md)).
Ship's `Meta` inherits `"abstract"` from Named's, on which the metaclass set it to `False` once it had made Named (`django/db/models/base.py:ModelBase.__new__`).

`"indexes"` and `"constraints"` are clones of the objects in `Options.indexes` and `Options.constraints`, where a placeholder in a name has been filled in and an index given no name has had one from the metaclass (`django/db/models/base.py:ModelBase._prepare`; [Constraints and indexes](../models/constraints.md)).

Every model state goes through `ModelState.__init__`: those `ModelState.from_model` makes, those `CreateModel` makes from its arguments, and every clone (`django/db/migrations/state.py:ModelState.__init__`).
`ProjectState.models` is a dictionary of model states, each under the pair of its application's label and its name in lower case (`django/db/migrations/state.py:ProjectState.__init__`).

The loader passes for it the labels of its unmigrated applications, whose models are not in `models`, though a graph with no node makes a state with none of those labels (`django/db/migrations/graph.py:MigrationGraph.make_state`; [Historical models: `StateApps` and rendering](historical-models.md)).

`ProjectState.__eq__` compares `models` and `real_apps` only, and `ModelState.__eq__` the label, the name, the options, the bases, the managers, and the fields pair by pair in the order of their names, each by what `Field.deconstruct` returns after the name (`django/db/migrations/state.py:ModelState.__eq__`, `django/db/models/fields/__init__.py:Field.deconstruct`).

`ProjectState.__eq__` compares `models` and `real_apps` only, and `ModelState.__eq__` the label, the name, the options, the bases, the managers, and the fields pair by pair in the order of their names, each by what `Field.deconstruct` returns after the name (`django/db/migrations/state.py:ModelState.__eq__`, `django/db/models/fields/__init__.py:Field.deconstruct`).

A model state's clone has dictionaries of its own for fields and options and a list of its own for managers, and in them the same field objects and option values (`django/db/migrations/state.py:ModelState.clone`).

Clones are how the state before a change is kept: `Migration.apply` clones the project state ahead of each operation's state half, and what that half changed inside a shared object would change in the from-state too (`django/db/migrations/migration.py:Migration.apply`).

The sharing reaches past clones: the fields `CreateModel` gives a model state are the operation's own objects, so one loader's project states share them until an operation replaces one (`django/db/migrations/operations/models.py:CreateModel.state_forwards`).

The state half of each operation that `django/db/migrations/operations/` has for a model, a field, an index or a constraint works by calling a method of the project state ([Operations: the base class and its two halves](operations.md)).

With `preserve_default=False`, `add_field` and `alter_field` file a clone of the field with its default set to `NOT_PROVIDED` (`django/db/migrations/state.py:ProjectState.add_field`; [The field operations, and those on indexes and constraints](field-operations.md)).

It does the same in each field that `get_references` finds, in any model state, pointing at the renamed field, where that field names its target's fields: `ForeignObject.to_fields` and, on a foreign key's rel, `ForeignObjectRel.field_name` (`django/db/migrations/state.py:ProjectState.rename_field`, `django/db/migrations/utils.py:get_references`).

It does the same in each field that `get_references` finds, in any model state, pointing at the renamed field, where that field names its target's fields: `ForeignObject.to_fields` and, on a foreign key's rel, `ForeignObjectRel.field_name` (`django/db/migrations/state.py:ProjectState.rename_field`, `django/db/migrations/utils.py:get_references`).

`ProjectState.rename_model`, for `RenameModel`, files a clone of the model state under the new key, with its `name` changed, puts a clone that names the new model in the place of each field `get_references` finds pointing at the old one, as its target or as a many-to-many field's through model, and then calls `remove_model` for the old key (`django/db/migrations/state.py:ProjectState.rename_model`).
`ProjectState.alter_model_options` puts a new dictionary in place of `options`, the old entries overlaid with those it is given (`django/db/migrations/state.py:ProjectState.alter_model_options`).

Each of the methods the operations call ends by seeing to the state's registry: if the state has been rendered, the historical models the change touches are taken out of it and, but for a model removed, rendered again from their model states (`django/db/migrations/state.py:ProjectState.reload_model`; [Historical models: `StateApps` and rendering](historical-models.md)).
A many-to-many field is entered under its target and, where it names a through model, under that too (`django/db/migrations/state.py:ProjectState.resolve_model_field_relations`).

The map's reader is the autodetector: `MigrationAutodetector._detect_changes` calls `resolve_fields_and_relations` on both of its states before it compares anything (`django/db/migrations/autodetector.py:MigrationAutodetector._detect_changes`; [The autodetector: comparing two project states](autodetector.md)).
